findings.title: 68 GB Stolen From a Philippine Government Agency's Overseas-Employment Databases, Exposed by the Operator's Own Open Directory
findings.summary_md: Hunt.io reported that an unknown operator copied 27 SQL Server backup files totaling 68.837 GiB matching Philippine overseas-employment and migrant-worker systems in 23 minutes 46 seconds on 6 September 2026. The operator left the working folder open on a staging server at 213.163.205.35 (UpCloud, Singapore) on port 80, serving 543 requests from 76 addresses over 16 hours. The directory contained a rebranded GodPotato privilege escalation tool, a PowerShell stager, two payloads, and a full Impacket environment.

findings.title: NPC probes alleged theft of 68GB of DMW-linked database backups
findings.summary_md: Newsbytes reported that the National Privacy Commission is investigating an alleged theft of 68GB of database backups linked to Philippine Department of Migrant Workers systems. The investigation follows an Oct. 28 report by Hunt.io, which said it recovered transfer logs showing 27 Microsoft SQL Server backup files totaling 68.837 GiB were copied on Sept. 6, 2026, in less than 24 minutes. Hunt.io traced two servers involved in subsequent file retrievals to government portal domains under dmw.gov.ph, and said it notified the relevant national computer emergency response team before publishing.

findings.title: 68 GB of stolen PH gov't data found online, says cybersecurity firm
findings.summary_md: Rappler summarized the Hunt.io finding, noting 27 SQL Server backups totaling 68.837 GB were copied on 6 September 2026. The National Privacy Commission is investigating and Philippine authorities are probing the suspected theft. Rappler emphasized that Hunt.io did not examine the contents of the backups, so the exact nature of potentially stolen files remains unconfirmed, though filenames point to migrant-worker administration systems.
